First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+(kx)^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(kx)+C
$$

We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{\infty }\frac{18}{4{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =18\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1/2}^{a}\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =18\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1/2}^{a}\frac{1}{(2x)^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =18\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x)]}_{1/2}^{a} \\  & =9\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)) \\  & =9\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =9\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)-\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x)=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x)=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/2ad762128a32c119f1783b88b4d10ae6820a914689296f03eedad206e097a29d.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{\infty }\frac{18}{4{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =9\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)-\frac{9\pi }{4} \\  & =9\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{9\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
